correctness.rationale: For k below every defining degree, the complete-intersection ideal has no degree-k element, so the restricted ambient forms give a base-point-free series with M=binom(N+k,k) independent sections and degree kD. The Wronskian line bundle has degree M(kD+(M-1)(g-1)); adjunction gives 2g-2=D(S-N-1). Modulo two, an even M makes the degree even, while an odd M removes the genus term. Kummer--Lucas gives M odd exactly when N and k have disjoint binary supports. The real corollary follows because non-real points of an effective real divisor occur in conjugate pairs.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete arithmetic phase law for a canonical geometric divisor across every low-order Veronese re-embedding of every smooth complete-intersection curve. It converts the Wronskian degree into a simple binary criterion and, over the reals, turns that criterion into a forced-existence theorem for inflection or hyperosculation. The admissible range is geometrically intrinsic: it is exactly the range before the defining ideal creates relations among ambient degree-k forms.
